To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

higher effort–reward ratio at the age of about 50 years predicted exit from the labor market before the age 61 years and this association was not explained by socioeconomic status or allostatic load and symptoms of depression.

stressful work conditions can be associated with exit from labour market at the early age of 61 or less, and that this is not explained by the socioeconomic position of individuals, or by the allostatic load or depression.

higher effort–reward imbalances and lower job control predicted exit from the labor market at the age 61 years and younger, and that the association of higher effort with exit from the labor force was independent of socioeconomic measures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the working conditions of employees influence their health and well-being.
the question of what are the psychosocial factors in work that predict exiting the labour market at a relatively young age.
work-related psychosomatic health in older workers and the risk of exiting the labour market at a younger age.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the psychosocial work environment may have an independent impact on exit from the labour force.
higher ERI and lower job control can be a risk factor for exit from the labour force before the age of the pension age.
the higher the effort–reward imbalance at work the more likely the individual will exit the labour market.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
higher ERI and lower job control can be a risk factor for early exit from the labour force.
higher effort–reward imbalances and lower job control can lead to exit from the workforce.
higher ERI and lower job control were associated with exit from labour market before age 61.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk for early retirement is not only related to socioeconomic position but that psychosocial factors such as effort–reward imbalance also play a role.
the risk factors for exit from the labour force are similar to those for exit from the work force, and that these risk factors are also similar to the risk factors for disability.
work-related factors can contribute to exit from the workforce before the age of retirement.
